title: Automated procedure for estimation of methylation levels in MS-HRM analysis
author: Sally Samsø Mathiasen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3ptqmnn
materials: Normalize the HRM curves using the Gene Scanning software (we recommend default settings for the normalization).

Export the difference plot as a text file. An example of layout of the file obtained from LightCycler480 instrument (Roche) see supplementary material S8-S11 File. IMPORTANT: The example of the calculations performed with Methylation Level Calculator (MLC) in this protocol (S2 File Methylation Levels Calculator (MLC)) requires experimental layout as described in Plate set up section of the MLC template, for other sample layouts in the experiment remember to modify the columns and rows names accordingly.
CALCULATION OF THE EXPRIMENT SPECIFIC DETECTION WINDOW

steps.title: Install Excel Solver Add‑in
steps.instruction: Install and enable the Solver Add‑in in Excel: on Mac go to Data → Analysis Tool, check Solver Add‑in and click OK; on PC go to File → Options → Add‑ins, click Go, check Solver Add‑in and click OK.

steps.title: Open Methylation Levels Calculator
steps.instruction: Open the Methylation Levels Calculator (MLC) Excel file supplied as S2 File (Methylation Levels Calculator (MLC)).

steps.title: Open LC480 exported text file
steps.instruction: Open the exported text file generated by the LC480 instrument (example files S10‑S11 MGMT assay text_without outliers).

steps.title: Paste data into Imported Data sheet
steps.instruction: Copy all data from the LC480 text file and paste it into the “imported data” sheet of the MLC starting at cell B3, making sure the sample names in rows 2 and 3 match the file and that the decimal separator used in the text file is the same as set in Excel. This procedure works only for the plate layout shown in the “plate set up” sheet; other layouts require column modifications in the MLC.

substeps.instruction: Select all data in the text file and copy.
In the MLC workbook, go to the “imported data” sheet and select cell B3.
Verify that the names in rows 2 and 3 agree with the file.
Confirm that the decimal separator in the file matches Excel’s setting.

steps.title: Check AUC values and outliers
steps.instruction: The MLC automatically calculates AUC for each control and sample and shows the values in row 1 of the “imported data” sheet. Verify that AUC values for replicates (coloured groups) are within an acceptable range; if a replicate is an obvious outlier, replace its value with 0 and note the sample name. If the sheet does not recalculate automatically, set Excel to Automatic calculation (Formulas → Calculation Options → Automatic).

substeps.instruction: Inspect AUC values for each replicate.
If a value is an outlier, change it to 0 and record the sample name.
If calculations do not update, enable Automatic calculation mode.

steps.title: Review 0‑variable calculations
steps.instruction: Navigate to the “0 variable” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates AUC for each control replicate, (2) uses Equation 1 to compute theoretical AUC for each methylation level based on the maximum AUC (0 % methylation control), and (3) plots the theoretical standard curve (blue) together with observed AUCs (red).

steps.title: Review 1‑variable calculations
steps.instruction: Navigate to the “1 variable” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates AUC for each control replicate, (2) applies Equation 2 with M = 1 to compute theoretical AUCs, and (3) plots the resulting standard curve.

steps.title: Solve for M using LSA
steps.instruction: Go to the “1 variable after LSA” sheet, open Solver (Data → Solver), click Solve, then OK. Solver performs least‑squares analysis to determine the optimal M value, recalculates the theoretical standard curve (blue) in panel 3, and updates all panels.

steps.title: Review 2‑variables calculations
steps.instruction: Navigate to the “2 variables” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates AUC for each control replicate, (2) uses Equation 3 with N = 1 to compute theoretical AUCs, and (3) plots the standard curve.

steps.title: Solve for M and N using LSA
steps.instruction: Go to the “2 variables after LSA” sheet, open Solver (Data → Solver), click Solve, then OK. Solver determines optimal M and N values by least‑squares analysis, updates the theoretical AUCs (Equation 3) and redraws the blue standard curve together with observed AUCs.

steps.title: Generate polynomial trend function
steps.instruction: Open the “Polynomial trend function (PTF)” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) transforms the theoretical standard curve from Equation 3 (AUC → methylation) because Excel cannot invert the function directly, (2) fits a 10‑degree polynomial to describe methylation level as a function of AUC, and (3) plots this polynomial (red).

steps.title: Calculate unknown sample methylation
steps.instruction: Go to the “Unknown sample calculation (USC)” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) lists each sample name, (2) calculates AUC for each sample replicate, and (3) computes methylation levels for the unknown samples using Equation 3 with the M and N values obtained earlier (via the transformation from the PTF sheet).

steps.title: Determine control cut‑off statistics
steps.instruction: Open the “Cut off (CO)” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates AUC for each control replicate, (2) computes standard deviation and mean for each control, and (3) plots the Gaussian distribution for each control. This operation may take a bit of time.

steps.title: Define detection window
steps.instruction: Navigate to the “Detection window” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates AUC, standard deviation, and mean for each control replicate, (2) calculates overlap between consecutive controls, (3) lists the controls in order, (4) highlights overlapping regions in pink, and (5) requires the user to enter the lower and upper limits of the detection window (percentage) in cells P7 and Q7. Example limits: upper = 60 % and 50 %; lower = 10 % and 5 %.

substeps.instruction: Review the calculated overlaps and highlighted regions.
Enter the desired lower limit (e.g., 10 % and 5 %) in cell P7.
Enter the desired upper limit (e.g., 60 % and 50 %) in cell Q7.

steps.title: Solve M and N within detection window
steps.instruction: Go to the “2 variables within DW” sheet. Ensure Excel calculation mode is Automatic (Formulas → Calculation Options → Automatic). Open Solver (Data → Solver), click Solve, then OK. Solver recalculates M and N values restricted to the assay‑specific detection window and updates the standard curve.

steps.title: Polynomial trend within detection window
steps.instruction: Open the “PTF within DW” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) calculates theoretical AUC from Equation 3 using the M and N values obtained for the detection window, and (2) fits and plots a 10‑degree polynomial trend (blue curve) for this range.

steps.title: Calculate unknowns within detection window
steps.instruction: Go to the “USC within DW” sheet. The MLC automatically (1) lists sample names, (2) calculates AUC for each sample replicate, and (3) computes methylation levels for the unknown samples using Equation 3 with the M and N values specific to the detection window.
